name: Sebastian Hoeneß
keynotes:
Not as impressive as initial results but underlying data suggests they have been unlucky in the 2024–25 season with strong numbers despite lower league position of 9th, 3rd for xPoints. Second senior job after a spell at Hoffenheim. Background was in youth coaching with RB Leipzig & Bayern Munich in ranging roles. Meets key attributes of providing entertaining but also results football, initially had taken Stuttgart from 18th in the Bundesliga to 2nd last season. Did demonstrate overperforming relative to resources and rival club quality. Stuttgart are also one the youngest teams in the Bundesliga since taking charge which makes his work more impressive and links with career path of working with younger players. In terms of playing style, Stuttgart control games. 
Pretty much fitting all the criteria for an up and coming coach; balance between defense & attack, working with younger players, controlled possession-passing build up style in an adaptable 4–2–3–1 / 4–4–2, strong press out of possession, results to back up performance levels in 2023–24 season and has shown ability in different scenarios already - got team out of a relegation battle & competing in the top end of the table. Hoffenheim sides in 2020–21 & 2021–22 in first managerial roles performed strongly too. All in still a high level coach who could get big job in England.

Consideration for Championship teams, interesting one. Over performance and style boxes ticked.

name: Eric Roy
keynotes: Incredible job at Brest significantly overachieving on resources in relation to performances and results on the pitch (This season squad value obviously increased with performances so figure looks lower on resource performance). Started in January 2023 while Brest were in 17th place, conceding 33 goals. Roy's biggest initial impact was defensive organization reducing Brest to conceding 21 Goals in his 21 first league games. Implemented a basic but very organized and structured deep 4–5–1 block in the initial phase with the sole objective of avoiding relegation. Impressive continuation from 2022–23 into 2023–24 as Eric Roy developed Brest's playing style to be more conducive of being effective across an entire season and be competitive in games and more proactive rather than initial fire fighting style. Marketable attributes for the Premier League in particular to be able to join mid season, get results quickly in struggling moments but then have the capacity to recognize, coach & develop playing style in the 2nd season finishing 3rd in Ligue 1.

Multiple examples of current elite level coaches starting their career in the lower tiers of Italy. Could be argued they typically develop through the Italian leagues rather than go international early and how that would work. However 1/2 interesting coaches is Matteo Andreoletti at Padova. Liked the look of Davide Possanzini at Matova in Serie C last season but has since been picked up by CAA Base. 
Usually these guys have mixed beginnings initially; Lecco (2013–2014) Started as a goalkeeper coach and youth team assistant. Seregno (2015–2018) Managed in Serie D, achieving respectable league finishes. Inveruno (2018–2019) Led the team to the Serie D playoffs. Sanremese (2021–2022) Reached playoff semifinals and finished second in the league the following season. Pro Sesto (2022–2023) Surprise finishing 4th in Serie C Group A. Knocked out by Vicenza in playoffs. Benevento (2023) Brief stint in Serie C ended after 6 months due to results. Just 36, influenced by both Gian Piero Gasperini & Roberto De Zerbi and plays a 3–4–3 dominant passing-possession style but also very attacking based. The Serie C is divided into three 20 club groups & Wyscout ranks out of all 60. Across all 60 teams Padova are a standout combination of playing style matched with balance between creating and preventing chances ultimately winning games of football.

name: Stevie Grieve
keynotes: 38 year old Scottish head coach in his first managerial role in Finland with some interesting notes, potentially a differential one to have for a League One / Two side. His SJK team are one of the youngest top flight teams in the world with an average age of 22.5, clear emphasis and coaching characteristic of youth and player development. Style and performance to add to this; balanced attack-defense, decent game control and press while overperforming resources.

name: Elias Charalambous
keynotes:
Impressive Europa League campaign finishing 11/36 teams, ahead of clubs like Ajax, Porto, Hoffenheim, Nice for a team of their quality. Domestically excellent too and a marketable combination to deliver expectation in their style within league but add different dynamic of being able to compete as underdogs in Europe to reach the round of 16. Good option to replace managers like Jindrich Trpisovsky at Slavia Prague etc or Sparta Prague. That type of move from Romania first before being more in the window for bigger European move. Minor roles in his homeland Cyprus previously but left-field coach doing good work in opening games as a manager. Style wise; Possession-Pressing accomplished in both attack & defense in the Superliga but varied flexibility as transitional, lower possession side in Europe. Back to back League Titles since joining in 2023.

name: Fredrik Holmberg
keynotes: New interesting head coach worth monitoring. Taken GAIS from the 3rd tier to 5th in the Allsvenskan. Significantly overperforming resources, balanced side both ways, style of play moderate possession & pressing. Lower Championship sides of interest.

name: Anders Torstensson
keynotes: Doing a great job at Mjallby and has them top of the table. Significant overperformance relative to expectation and resources. Underlying data not as impressive. Seems one-club man type though; involved with Mjallby nearly 20+ years

name: BJ Callaghan
keynotes: Ex US national team assistant doing great job in first managerial role. Overperforming expectation with balance both ways. No particular style indicators.

name: Mikey Varas
keynotes: Former USA U20 coach & ex-assistant of the US senior team. Notable opening season as a number one; attacking, possession-pressing style with substance in the league table.

name: Bradley Carnell
keynotes: Another inexperienced coach doing very well early days. Former assistant of Gerhard Struber and style resembles this; highest intensity press in the MLS with a vertical, direct low-possession build up.

name: Mitch Kniat
keynotes: Interesting one. Took over Bielefield in Germany after they suffered back-to-back relegations from Bundesliga-3.Liga. Club in freefall, 22 new players in 23-24 but kept up with youngest non-B team in 3.Liga & underlying numbers had them 3rd vs 15th. Won the league the following season with a style substance & very young squad. Also got to cup final beating 4 Bundesliga teams, inc. Alonso’s Leverkusen. Stable start to 25-26 2.Bundesliga season.

name: Victor Sanchez
keynotes: Won the league in Slovenia with Olimpija last season before joining Croatia side Rijeka in the summer. Hasn’t done brilliantly in Croatia yet but good credentials for certain contexts based on previous roles. Stabilized clubs like Betis, Deportivo, Malaga. Won titles. Organizer-structured based coach. Could be a good option as a national team coach for smaller nations or club level at some of the bigger sides.

name: Juan Carlos Carcedo
keynotes: Unai Emery’s ex-assistant doing notable job in Cyprus with Pafos. Won the league last season for the first time in Pafos’ history, currently competing above expectation in the Champions League. At Zaragoza & Ibiza in Spain before. Attractive option for big clubs in Asia.

name: Gonzalo Garcia
keynotes: Good start at Hajduk Split in Croatia; competing with Dinamo Zagreb and 2nd in table. Formerly Istra coach where he did solid stability job with a young side. Had spells in Portugal with Arouca and started career at FC Twente. Could be interesting candidate for jobs East

name: Ruslan Rotan
keynotes: Noticed due to overperformance in leading small club FC Oleksandriya to 2nd place ahead of Shakhtar in Ukraine last season, just 3 points off 1st place Kiev. Changed club and has Polissaya competing for top spot while former club has plummeted down the table. Interesting one, ex-Ukraine U21-U23 coach.

name: Jurgen Samuel
keynotes: Won the Austrian Bundesliga with Sturm Graz last season. Pressing-Attacking style of play. First senior role, was a youth coach before. Did overperform underlying numbers but impressive title win over RB Salzburg.

name: Rulani Mokwena
keynotes: Very left-field pick; one of the best up & coming African head coaches who recall doing notable work with Mamelodi Sundowns in the South African Premiership between 2021-2024. Won x4 titles in four seasons and set a record for consecutive titles. Style based coach with interesting build up patterns. Impressive pressing-possession numbers, clear detailed coaching & style with consistent winning. Won 8/9 games so far in Algeria. Interesting avenue for international manager market.
